findings.message: the pattern matches 6 of 7 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is 'Feb  8 07:16:20 intranet-server sshd[28030]: Did not receive identification string from 10.237.1.238 port 49844'. Of the 8 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{SYSLOGTIMESTAMP:hdr_time} %{HOSTNAME:hostname} %{DATA:proc}\\[%{POSINT:pid}\\]:\\s+%{WORD:msg_word}\\s+user\\s+%{NOTSPACE:'. the pattern matches up to %{NOTSPACE:user_name}, which fails on 'not receive identification string from 1'. %{WORD} matches letters, digits and underscore only - NOT a dot, hyphen, colon or slash. For a hostname use %{HOSTNAME}, for any run of non-space characters use %{NOTSPACE} If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

the IR maps 'reason_text', but no pattern captures it: the patterns capture only 'action_word', 'command', 'cwd', 'gid', 'group_name', 'hdr_time', 'home', 'hostname', 'method', 'msg_word', 'owner_uid', 'pid', 'proc', 'rest', 'shell', 'src_ip', 'src_port', 'tty', 'user_id', 'user_name'. A mapping whose key is never extracted leaves its ECS field empty on every line. Add a named capture for each of these keys where its value sits in the line, or move the key to `unresolved`.
